description: Org-level security standards: authentication, authorization, input validation, output encoding, secret handling, dependency hygiene, and safe server behaviour that apply to every project installing AI Agile.

standards.title: Authorization-check functions run in a fixed, trusted execution context
standards.description: Any function that performs a role or authorization check runs in a fixed, trusted execution context that a caller cannot subvert: it does not resolve names, permissions, or state through caller-controlled configuration, and cannot be tricked into running privileged logic in an attacker-influenced scope.
standards.rationale: Authorization logic that resolves through caller-controlled context (mutable resolution paths, shadowable names, session settings) can be subverted to escalate privilege; pinning the execution context closes that class of attack.
acceptance_criteria: Authorization-check functions in the diff pin their execution context and do not depend on caller-controlled configuration to resolve names, permissions, or state.
No authorization function can be redirected to attacker-controlled definitions via a mutable resolution path.
anti_patterns: An authorization-check function that resolves referenced objects through a caller-controllable resolution path or mutable session setting.

standards.title: Enforce record-level authorization at the data layer
standards.description: Access to stored records is authorized at the data layer -- record/row-level access controls enforced by the data store or data-access layer -- not solely by application code. Read and write access is gated by the caller's identity and role, default-deny. (Row-level security policies are one such mechanism.)
standards.rationale: Authorization enforced only in application code is bypassed by any path that reaches the data directly; enforcing it at the data layer makes it hold regardless of the caller.
acceptance_criteria: Every stored entity in the diff is protected by record/row-level access controls at the data layer, default-deny.
Write access is gated by the caller's role at the data layer, not only in application code.
anti_patterns: A table or collection whose access is enforced only by application code, with no record-level authorization at the data layer.

standards.title: Contextually encode untrusted content at every output boundary
standards.description: User-supplied (untrusted) content must be neutralised for the context it is written into — choose the encoder that matches the sink. This standard governs the HTML and email-header sinks: HTML output (web or email body) escapes user values via escapeHtml() or the framework's auto-escaping (never raw interpolation or dangerouslySetInnerHTML with unescaped content); email subjects/headers strip CR/LF via safeHeaderField() and are built through the templating library, never string concatenation. Other sinks follow the same principle under their own standards — PDFs/reports (STD-SEC-008), error responses (STD-SEC-009), exports incl. SQL/URL (STD-SEC-012).
standards.rationale: Untrusted content interpreted in the wrong context is the root of injection (XSS, email header injection, phishing); encoding for the specific sink neutralises it, and the correct defence is always contextual.
acceptance_criteria: Every user-supplied value written into HTML (web or email body) in the diff passes through escapeHtml() or framework auto-escaping, never raw interpolation.
Every value interpolated into an email subject/header in the diff is CR/LF-stripped via safeHeaderField() and built via the templating library, not string concatenation.
No diff writes untrusted content into an HTML or email-header context without the context-appropriate encoder (other sinks follow STD-SEC-008 / STD-SEC-009 / STD-SEC-012).
anti_patterns: `subject: 'Report for ' + userName` interpolated without safeHeaderField().
Embedding a freeform user response into an HTML body without escapeHtml().
`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` fed unescaped user content.

standards.title: Pin all dependencies to exact versions
standards.description: Every third-party dependency is pinned to a specific exact version — never a range or an unpinned name — across all package manifests and inline imports, with a committed lockfile.
standards.rationale: Unpinned or range dependencies resolve to whatever version is current at build time, introducing supply-chain and reproducibility risk; exact pins make builds deterministic and reviewable.
acceptance_criteria: Every dependency introduced or modified in the diff is pinned to an exact version (no range, no bare name).
the server runtime npm: specifiers in the diff include a full patch version (name@x.y.z); package.json entries use exact versions, not ^/~ ranges.
A dependency change in the diff updates and commits the lockfile.
anti_patterns: `import React from 'npm:react@18'` or `'npm:zod'` with no version.
`"react": "^18.3.0"` (caret range) in package.json instead of an exact version.

standards.title: Treat user content as untrusted when rendering PDFs and reports
standards.description: Generated PDFs and reports carry user-authored freeform content. The generator must treat that content as untrusted: escape or strip control characters, never execute embedded JavaScript, and never interpolate user content into an executable or markup context unescaped.
standards.rationale: Even though PDF renderers are less XSS-prone than HTML email clients, user content in a report is still untrusted input and must be neutralised.
acceptance_criteria: User-authored values rendered into a PDF/report in the diff are escaped or sanitised (control characters stripped) before rendering.
No diff path lets user content reach a JavaScript-execution or unescaped-markup context in the report generator.
Report templates in the diff interpolate user values through the escaping/sanitising helper, not raw.
anti_patterns: Injecting a raw freeform response into report markup without escaping.
A report template that evaluates user-supplied content as script.

standards.title: Sanitise all error responses — never leak internals to clients
standards.description: Errors surfaced to a client expose only a generic, safe message; internal details — raw exception messages, stack traces, SQL, server internals — are logged server-side but never returned to the client.
standards.rationale: Raw error messages and stack/SQL fragments disclose internal structure and aid attackers; users need a translated, safe message.
acceptance_criteria: server endpoint error responses in the diff return a generic message (e.g. via errorResponse()) and log details with console.error, not `error.message` to the client.
No diff returns a stack trace or SQL string in a client response body.
Frontend error display in the diff routes through formatthe databaseError()/formatError() (or a provided userMessage), never raw error text.
anti_patterns: `return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: error.message }), { status: 500 })`.
Rendering a caught Postgres error directly into a toast or page.

standards.title: Validate CORS origins against an allowlist — never a wildcard
standards.description: Cross-origin responses use a single, centrally-defined CORS configuration that validates the request Origin against an allowlist, never returns a wildcard `*`, and includes `Vary: Origin`.
standards.rationale: A single validated CORS source prevents unauthorised cross-origin access; wildcard origins open the API to any site, and a missing Vary: Origin enables cache poisoning.
acceptance_criteria: server endpoint CORS in the diff comes from _shared/cors.ts, not inline header literals.
No diff sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: '*'`.
Origin whitelist changes in the diff are confined to _shared/cors.ts, and responses include Vary: Origin.
anti_patterns: `'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*'` in any function.
Defining per-function CORS headers instead of importing the shared utility.

standards.title: Default to least-privilege credentials; elevated credentials are a governed exception
standards.description: Data access uses least-privilege, authorization-respecting credentials by default, so access controls apply to every request. Elevated or service-level credentials that bypass those controls are a governed exception -- used only where explicitly required, scoped narrowly, and justified.
standards.rationale: Running under least privilege ensures authorization is enforced on every operation; routine use of elevated credentials silently disables those controls.
acceptance_criteria: Data access in the diff uses the least-privilege, authorization-respecting credentials by default.
Any use of elevated/service credentials is explicitly justified and scoped to the narrow operation that requires it.
anti_patterns: Performing routine data access with an elevated/service credential that bypasses authorization controls.

standards.title: Sanitise and validate all data on export
standards.description: Data emitted from the application into an external format (exports, generated SQL/markup/CSV/XML) is sanitised and escaped for that destination: user content in SQL output is escaped or parameterised, URLs are scheme-validated (http/https only), and free text is cleaned of control characters.
standards.rationale: Exports turn stored user content into executable SQL/markup downstream; unsanitised values enable SQL injection and malformed output.
acceptance_criteria: User-supplied values in new export paths in the diff pass through the appropriate sanitiser before output.
SQL export in the diff escapes all interpolated values via escapeSqlValue() rather than raw string concatenation.
URL fields in export paths in the diff are validated to http/https only.
anti_patterns: Concatenating a raw `domain_name` into an INSERT statement without escapeSqlValue().
Emitting an unvalidated `javascript:`/`file:` URL into an export.

standards.title: Read secrets from the environment; never hardcode or commit them
standards.description: Secrets — API keys, auth tokens, service-role/DB credentials, signing secrets — are read at runtime from the environment/secret store, never written as string literals in source, never committed (.env stays gitignored), and never emitted into logs, error responses, comments, or test fixtures.
standards.rationale: A hardcoded or committed secret leaks permanently through git history and client bundles and cannot be un-disclosed by deletion.
acceptance_criteria: Secrets used in the diff are read via the environment.get() (Edge) and do not appear as string literals.
No diff commits a secret value (key/token/password/service-role key) in source, config, fixture, or comment, and .env remains gitignored.
No secret value is written to a console log or returned in an error response in the diff.
anti_patterns: `const SERVICE_KEY = "eyJ..."` or an API key literal in source.
Committing a populated .env file or pasting a token into a test fixture.
`console.log('using key', apiKey)`.

standards.title: Validate external input at the boundary before use
standards.description: All externally-supplied input — request bodies, URL/query parameters, headers, and routing fields — is validated against an explicit schema at the boundary before any database or business logic runs; invalid or unknown input is rejected (e.g. 400), never silently coerced.
standards.rationale: Unvalidated input reaches the database and business logic and is the entry point for injection and malformed-state bugs; validating at the boundary fails fast and keeps internal code working with known-good shapes.
acceptance_criteria: A new server endpoint in the diff validates its request payload (Zod schema / validateRequest) before any DB call or business logic.
the data-access layer-style handlers in the diff validate `object` and `action` and reject unknown entity types with a 400 before touching the database.
Externally-supplied values in the diff are validated/parsed, not passed unchecked into queries or writes.
anti_patterns: Using fields off `await req.json()` directly without validating the shape.
Accepting an arbitrary `object` string and querying with it before confirming it is a known entity.

standards.title: Authenticate and authorize every protected endpoint before business logic
standards.description: Every server endpoint that reads or writes protected data authenticates the caller and authorizes the specific action before any business logic or data access runs. Authentication and authorization are the first step, not an afterthought.
standards.rationale: Running business logic or touching data before the caller is authenticated and authorized exposes protected operations to unauthorised callers.
acceptance_criteria: Every protected endpoint in the diff authenticates the caller and authorizes the specific action before any business logic or data access.
No protected handler performs work before its auth check.
anti_patterns: A protected endpoint that runs a query or mutation before authenticating and authorizing the caller.

standards.title: Log security-relevant events without leaking secrets or PII
standards.description: Authentication outcomes, authorization denials, and other security-significant actions are logged with enough non-sensitive context to investigate (actor as a Display ID, action, timestamp, request id), and security-relevant errors are recorded rather than silently swallowed. Log statements never include secrets, credentials, tokens, full PII, or raw request bodies (see STD-SEC-013, STD-ARCH-022).
standards.rationale: Without security-event logs, intrusion and abuse are undetectable and un-investigable (OWASP A09; NIST CSF Detect); conversely, logging secrets or PII turns the log into a new disclosure surface.
acceptance_criteria: Authentication failures and authorization denials in the diff are logged with non-sensitive context (actor Display ID, action, request id).
No log statement in the diff writes a secret, token, password, full PII value, or raw request body.
Security-relevant errors in the diff are recorded (server log), not silently swallowed.
anti_patterns: A 401/403 path that returns with no log of the failure.
`console.log(req.headers.authorization)` or logging a full payload containing PII.

standards.title: Scan dependencies for known vulnerabilities
standards.description: The dependency set is checked against known-vulnerability databases (e.g. npm audit or equivalent) as part of CI. A dependency newly added or upgraded in a diff must not carry an unaddressed high/critical advisory unless the PR documents the accepted risk and why no fix is applied.
standards.rationale: Exact version pins (STD-SEC-007) make builds deterministic but a pinned version can still be vulnerable; scanning surfaces known CVEs so they are patched rather than shipped.
acceptance_criteria: A dependency added or upgraded in the diff has no known unaddressed high/critical advisory, or the PR documents the accepted risk.
A dependency vulnerability scan runs in CI against the committed lockfile.
Scanner findings are triaged, not suppressed wholesale to make CI pass.
anti_patterns: Adding a dependency with a known critical CVE and no mitigation or documented acceptance.
Disabling the audit/scan step to get a green build.

standards.title: Validate uploaded files -- type, size, and content
standards.description: User-uploaded files are validated before storage and before rendering: enforce an allowlist of accepted types, a maximum size, and content checks appropriate to the type (e.g. verifying the bytes match the claimed type). Untrusted file content is never rendered or executed without validation.
standards.rationale: Unvalidated uploads enable oversized payloads, type spoofing, and malicious content that is later served to other users.
acceptance_criteria: Uploaded files in the diff are checked against a type allowlist and a maximum size before storage.
File content is validated to match its claimed type before it is stored or rendered.
anti_patterns: Storing or rendering an uploaded file without validating its type, size, and content.

standards.title: Guard server-side outbound requests against SSRF
standards.description: Server-side HTTP requests whose destination is influenced by user input restrict the target: allowlist the host and scheme (e.g. https only), reject internal, loopback, and link-local addresses, and do not follow redirects to disallowed targets.
standards.rationale: Unrestricted server-side requests to user-influenced destinations allow SSRF -- reaching internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or arbitrary hosts.
acceptance_criteria: Server-side outbound requests in the diff with user-influenced destinations validate the host and scheme against an allowlist.
Internal, loopback, and link-local targets are rejected.
anti_patterns: Making a server-side HTTP request to a user-supplied URL without host/scheme allowlisting or internal-address blocking.
